newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Bisnis Indonesia's survey of the twenty biggest capitalised stocks on the Jakarta Stock Exchange shows average earnings growth of almost 40 percent.
The Indonesian government offficially closed down the boatpeople camp on Galang Island, south of Singapore. The last Vietnamese boatpeople were repatriated last week.

The Capital Market Supervisiory Agency (Bapepam) has opposed Intisetia Tritunggal's bid to take over a majority stake in Telagamas Pertiwi, a manufacturer of sports shoes. It did not give any reasons.
The government said that the decision of loyalist supporters of ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, to open a new office is unacceptable.
Around 2,000 of the controversial Timor cars arrived from South Korea yesterday by ship. The cars will be sold by PT Timor Putra Nasional, a company owned by one of President Suharto's sons.
